newsitem.title: CHINA: SOCCER-TOP CHINA LEAGUE TO RESTART ON SUNDAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TOP CHINA LEAGUE TO RESTART ON SUNDAY.

text.p: The 1997 Chinese first division soccer league will kick off this weekend with a clash between defending champions Dalian Wanda and newly promoted Vanguard Huandao, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

While Dalian's squad included seven Chinese international players, their upstart opponents would be led by former national team coach German Klaus Schlappner for the first game of the season on Sunday, the agency said.
Players from all 12 first division teams had been on a tough winter training programme since the end of the 1996 league last October, it said.
State media said winter training at high altitudes in mountainous southwestern Yunnan province was aimed at focusing players to boost the quality of league soccer.
Players were forced to run up to 12 km (seven miles) a day and banned from using mobile telephones or receiving visitors.
"Now... each of the 12 teams participating in this year's league will try their best to prove to the fans that it deserves their support," Xinhua said.
Qingdao Hainiu will join the first division along with Vanguard Huandao after the relegation last year of Guangzhou Songri and Shenzhen.

On Sunday, Beijing Guo'an would play Sichuan Quanxing; Shanghai Shenhua would play Yanbian Aodong; Vanguard Huandao would play Dalian Wanda; Tianjin Lifei would play Chinese Army; Jinan Taishan would play Qingdao Hainiu and Guangzhou Apollo would play Guangdong Hongyuan, Xinhua said.
